references.text: God commands Moses to carve two new stone tablets after the first ones were broken, referring back to the original account in Deut. 10:1.
The instructions for building the ark of the covenant from acacia wood, which Moses was commanded to make in Deut. 10:1.
Moses breaks the first stone tablets in anger over the golden calf, necessitating the new tablets mentioned in Deut. 10:1.
Moses goes up the mountain and receives the Ten Commandments written on the tablets, paralleling the command in Deut. 10:1.
The earlier account of the first stone tablets that Moses received on the mountain, providing context for the renewal in chapter 10.
Confirms that the ark contained only the two stone tablets that Moses placed there at Horeb, as noted in Deut. 10:1-5.
Mentions the ark of the covenant and the stone tablets with the Ten Commandments, referring to the Old Testament account including Deut. 10:1.
